newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 claws back losses, ends nearly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 claws back losses, ends nearly unchanged.

text.p: The UK's leading blue chip stock index ended nearly unchanged, near the day's best level, after an early wave of profit-taking.
The benchmark FTSE 100 index fell 3.2 points to 4,337.8, with decliners outpacing advancers 55 to 41.
Turnover was relatively light, capped by Wall Street closed for a national holiday. At 1643 GMT, SEAQ volume registered 629.0 million shares.
UK shares started the day on a weak note after the Dow pulled back below the 7,000 mark on Friday
With no direction from the U.S. and no corporate or economic reports out today, many participants just stood on the sidelines, dealers said.
The initial burst fit-taking was prompted by the Dow closing below the 7,000 mark, dealers said.
Worries that UK and U.S. equity markets were over-extended after last week's surge also encouraged profit-taking, they said.

Caution ahead of this evening's parliamentary vote on the mad cow crisis which may prompt a vote of no-confidence vote in the government unnerved some investors, though political analysts expect the government to survive.

"I'd say people are keeping a watchful eye on the political situation," said UK equity strategist Robert Buckland of HSBC James Capel. "But anyone who has let politics influence their investment decisions during the last six months must be in the bottom percentile."
Yet stock strategists and dealers agreed that at some point, politics will begin to take their toll on UK shares.
"One day it will dawn on the market that there's going to be a change in government, and the market probably will get quite choppy as a result," Buckland added.
But for the time being, investors were focusing on the raft of corporate results, due in upcoming weeks.

Unilever Plc, which reported a 15 percent rise in its annual profits on Friday, saw its shares surge. They were among the best performers on the FTSE 100, jumping 67-1/2p to 1605, tracking big gains in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in the Anglo-Dutch consumer products group in New York on Friday.
The ADRs closed on Friday at $188-1/4, up $8-1/4, boosted by a rise in profits and the planned sale of its speciality chemicals units, traders said.
"The stock was well bid in the U.S. on Friday. We're just seeing London play catch-up," one dealer said.
Shares in Rank Group Plc rebounding from recent weakness ahead of the leisure group's annual results on Thursday, dealers said.
The stock, which has underperformed the rest of the UK market by more than 20 percent over the past year, advanced 10p to 421-1/2.
Shares in Lloyds TSB Group Plc added 15p higher at 518-1/2p, having reached a record at 520p, after analysts met the company and some decided to increase their 1997 pretax profit estimates.

Following the meeting which analysts described as "positive" and "impressive", analysts were grouping around the 3.0 billion stg mark for the bank's 1997 profit and some were also raising earnings per share and dividend forecasts.
Shares in Cable & Wireless Plc CW L dropped 12p to 508-1/2 on profit-taking after recent gains and as the company's Mercury unit said it would cut the cost of international phone calls, dealers said.

The stock touched its highest level since May 1996, driven by an increase in Merrill Lynch's price target for the stock and renewed talk of global alliances in the telecoms business. --London newsroom +44-171-542-4026
